free_tier.stated: Free, no published per-dataset or per-account cap. 'Is this service free to use? Yes!' A 6.4 TB dataset has been deposited (staged incrementally).
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: per-object-cap: none published; the real cap is a transient staging worker ('files are stored on a worker with relatively limited storage space'), so very large datasets must be uploaded in batches with ~24 h waits between snapshots. Retention: permanent, every version gets its own DOI; 36-month grace before forced CC0 release

egress.terms: Free and anonymous. Objects live on Amazon S3 (`s3.amazonaws.com/openneuro.org`), public-read, ranged, CORS-open. No auth, no egress meter.

tooling: Openneuro-cli (`openneuro upload`) + git-annex, and DataLad. Read side is plain anonymous S3 GET. Any S3 client, rclone's s3 remote with no credentials, or plain curl.
chaining: Unlimited datasets, each a fresh S3 prefix under `openneuro.org/ds<ID>/`. Because the read side is unauthenticated S3, fetch volume never touches OpenNeuro's app tier.
limits_note: per-object-cap: none published; the real cap is a transient staging worker ('files are stored on a worker with relatively limited storage space'), so very large datasets must be uploaded in batches with ~24 h waits between snapshots. Retention: permanent, every version gets its own DOI; 36-month grace before forced CC0 release. Binding read limit is per-ip-shaping but weak.

reliability_note: Large uploads fail in the staging area and require batch-then-wait choreography; BIDS format is mandatory and undeface-d datasets get deleted after the fact.
